transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, it's nice to meet you too. I'm here because... my sleep has just become completely unmoored lately. 

At first, a little while ago, I was waking up after maybe two or three hours of sleep, but I'd get right up and start drafting plans. I actually felt completely ready to go. But now it's shifted. Now I just lie awake for hours before dawn. My stomach gets all tight, and I just... I don't get any sense of rest at all anymore.
During that time when you were sleeping only two or three hours and still felt ready to go, did you feel unusually energized or unusually irritable?

Well, honestly, it was a bit of both. For weeks I felt... almost brilliantly optimistic. It was as if every obstacle in my way was just completely trivial. 

But at the same time, if anyone questioned me or my plans, I got very irritable. I snapped at them. It honestly felt like they were trying to sabotage the only sensible man in the room.
During that energized period, did you have beliefs that other people said were clearly untrue or impossible?

Well, I didn't think they were impossible, but... my family certainly did. I truly believed I could fix my retirement accounts, advise three different start-ups, and completely overhaul the local arts council to make it a regional powerhouse. It just felt like my judgment was suddenly superior to everyone else's, and I couldn't understand why they thought I was being unrealistic.
During that energized period, did you hear voices or see things that other people could not?

No, no, I never had anything like that. I didn't hear any voices or see anything that wasn't there. It was really just the intense energy and the ideas, not anything playing tricks on my eyes or ears.
During that energized period, were you hospitalized because of your behavior or mental state?
No, I wasn't. I mean, my family was certainly very concerned about what I was doing, but... no, it never came to that. I wasn't put in a hospital or anything like that.
During that energized period, were you able to keep up with your usual work and responsibilities?

No, I wasn't. I mean, at the time I thought I was getting so much done, but... things actually fell apart. My wife has had to step in and completely take over our finances, and she feels she needs to stay with me now just for my safety. And as for my normal routine... I've just stopped showing up reliably for my commitments at the museum and the arts council. I haven't even been keeping up with my friends. So, no, I really wasn't managing my actual responsibilities at all.
During that energized period, did you feel absolutely certain you had special abilities or powers that other people simply could not recognize?

Well, I didn't think I had magical powers or anything like that. But I did feel... I guess I truly believed I was capable of doing things no one else could. I was convinced I could completely repair my retirement accounts, advise three different start-ups all at once, and turn the local arts council into this huge regional powerhouse. It was like I suddenly felt my judgment and my abilities were just far superior to everyone else's around me. I just felt absolutely certain I could do it all.
At that time, did you believe you had special powers?

No, like I just said, I didn't think I had magical powers or anything supernatural. I just felt incredibly capable, like my skills and judgment were better than anyone else's, but not... not actual superpowers.
At the time, were you completely convinced those plans were definitely achievable even when other people showed you clear evidence they were not?

Yes, I was. I mean, like I mentioned a moment ago, I truly believed I could pull all of it off—repairing the retirement accounts, advising those three start-ups, turning the arts council into a regional powerhouse. When my wife or anyone else tried to point out that the numbers didn't make sense or that it wasn't realistic, I just ignored them. I really felt like my judgment was suddenly superior to everyone else's, so I didn't care what their evidence showed. I was absolutely certain I was right.
At that time, were you completely unable to consider the possibility that you might be wrong?

I guess... I just didn't think I was wrong. It wasn't that I couldn't consider it, I just didn't see any reason to. I felt so sure of myself and what I was doing that the idea of being wrong didn't really cross my mind.
About how long did that unusually energized and irritable period last?

It lasted for about five months. After the investment loss happened, I just... I wasn't living like my usual retired self anymore. Everything I did during that whole five-month stretch revolved around trying to undo the damage.
Right now, are you feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel depressed right now, not most of the day or every day. I'm just here trying to figure all this out.
During that period, did you believe with complete certainty that your financial and leadership abilities were far beyond what was actually possible for you?

Yes, I really did. I honestly thought I could just... fix everything. I truly believed I had the ability to repair my retirement accounts, advise three different start-ups, and somehow turn the arts council into this massive regional powerhouse all at the same time. It just felt like my judgment was suddenly superior to everyone else's.
